transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sarah Patel (Redwood AE), Tom Nguyen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Maya Thompson (BrightBridge Head of Data), Evan Li (BrightBridge DevOps Manager), Priya Singh (BrightBridge Security Lead), Carlos Romero (BrightBridge Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated - may be imperfect):
- Onboarding kickoff; discussion of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options; key ask: SOC 2 + data residency, SSO/SAML, KMS integration.

- Customer requested a short Dedicated trial and an SE deep dive on private deployment networking (VPC details).

Topics: onboarding timeline, security/compliance, deployment options, pilot scope, telemetry and cost estimates

Transcript:
[00:00] Sarah Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, this is Sarah from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, joining me is Tom our solutions engineer and Lena our CSM, thanks for making time.
[00:08] Maya Thompson: Thanks Sarah, yes excited to kick this off, we, we want to move quickly but obviously security is top of mind.
[00:15] Evan Li: Hey all, Evan here, quick note we manage infra in AWS us-east-1 and we have some VPC peering constraints with our analytics account.
[00:23] Tom Nguyen: Got it, thanks, Tom from Redwood SE, we'll definitely need to understand the network boundaries for Private or Dedicated, and we can show patterns for Hosted that avoid egress of PHI.
[00:34] Priya Singh: Hi, Priya, Security — SOC2 is a big item for us, also KMS integration for customer-managed keys and audit logs retention.
[00:42] Carlos Romero: Carlos from Product, we care about latency for interactive features, target p95 under 600ms if possible.
[00:50] Sarah Patel: Great, I'm going to run through the onboarding agenda quickly: timeline, roles and responsibilities, pilot scope/metrics, security checklist, and next steps.
[00:58] Sarah Patel: Our standard onboarding playbook is usually 4-6 weeks to go from kickoff to pilot if there are no major network constraints, that includes account setup, SSO, test dataset, and a small Dedicated capacity or hosted trial.
[01:12] Maya Thompson: That timeline works but we may need to compress given product roadmap for September. Is there a way to accelerate?
[01:18] Tom Nguyen: We can parallelize a few things — security questionnaire and SSO setup can happen while we do initial perf sizing. Also for latency sensitive flows we can do a short Dedicated trial to validate p95 and throughput.
[01:29] Evan Li: For Dedicated trial, what's the typical provisioning lead time? We can't change infra easily on short notice.
[01:35] Tom Nguyen: For our Redwood Dedicated pools we generally can provision a small test pool in 3-5 business days once the contract is signed and capacity agreed. If you need private/on-prem it may be longer.
[01:45] Priya Singh: Can you walk through encryption at rest and KMS options? We manage keys and need to see key rotation policies, HSM integration possibilities.
[01:54] Tom Nguyen: Sure — we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Dedicated with VPC peering; hosted has envelope encryption with redwood-managed keys by default but we can offer CMKs for enterprise tiers. I'll share the KMS doc — but note the transcript auto system sometimes writes K M S as K M S, sorry for the, uh, noise.
[02:10] Maya Thompson: Also want to confirm data residency. We have EU patient records and need assurance that inference and logs do not leave region.
[02:18] Sarah Patel: Yes, we have region-restricted hosting and also Private deployment options where the control plane can be in your VPC or on-prem. For EU residency we can pin the region for inference and storage. We'll include the residency options in the playbook.
[02:31] Carlos Romero: On cost, do you have an estimate for token costs and Dedicated monthly commits? We need ballpark for procurement.
[02:38] Sarah Patel: We'll share a pricing sheet; for pilots we typically do usage-based with an optional short-term Dedicated commit to guarantee latency. Tom, maybe give quick note on typical unit economics?
[02:47] Tom Nguyen: Sure — rough numbers depend on model family and quantization; for a mid-size open model with int8 quant we usually see X tokens/sec at Y cost, but I'll run your workload numbers and give a Dedicated sizing and cost delta.
[02:59] Evan Li: We'll send sample traffic pattern, average and peak RPS, and some example prompts.
[03:05] Maya Thompson: Action item — we'll also include a sample of PII tags / classification so you can advise on redaction and caching policies.
[03:13] Sarah Patel: Perfect. For rollout plan — Lena will manage the project plan and weekly check-ins — we typically do a canary then ramp plan with monitoring hooks in the console.
[03:23] Lena Ortiz: I'll create the onboarding project in our CSM tool, invite stakeholders and set up a weekly 30 minute sync.
[03:29] Priya Singh: On audit logs and retention — we need 7 years retention for some records, is that supported?
[03:36] Tom Nguyen: Long retention is supported in Private deployments and some enterprise Hosted plans; you can export logs to your S3 bucket for compliance, or we can configure extended retention if you have the right tier. I'll include export examples in the docs.
[03:49] Maya Thompson: One more technical thing — we use redis for caching today, how does Redwood's KV cache integrate or is it separate?
[03:57] Tom Nguyen: We have a built-in KV cache in the runtime, but you can layer external caches for prefix caching. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your internal cache via VPC peering, though sometimes folks maintain a light redis mirror. We'll include architecture examples.
[04:14] Carlos Romero: For the pilot success criteria let's be explicit: p95 latency under 600ms for interactive flows, <10% regression in answer quality vs baseline, and cost per 1k tokens under threshold.
[04:25] Sarah Patel: Agreed — we'll capture those metrics and include eval prompt set suggestions.
[04:30] Evan Li: About SSO — we use Okta with SAML, need SSO for console and audit role mapping.
[04:36] Lena Ortiz: We support SAML/Okta — we'll send the SSO integration guide and a sample IdP metadata file.
[04:43] Priya Singh: Also RBAC and least privilege — want to ensure separation between dev and ops accounts.
[04:48] Tom Nguyen: We have RBAC with role-level permissions and can map to your SSO groups.
[04:53] Sarah Patel: Cool, quick recap of next steps: Sarah will share onboarding playbook, SSO and KMS docs, and the pricing sheet by Friday 2026-07-30. Tom will run perf estimates once we get the sample prompts and traffic. Lena will create the onboarding project and schedule weekly check-ins. Priya will send completed security questionnaire and SOC2 scope.
[05:12] Maya Thompson: Sounds good — we'll get the traffic and PII classification over by Friday.
[05:18] Carlos Romero: Can we also get a separate SE deep dive on private networking? Evan and I will join that.
[05:24] Tom Nguyen: Yes, I'll propose times for the private deployment deep dive — likely next week 2026-08-04 as discussed.
[05:32] Sarah Patel: Thank you all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs. Any final questions?
[05:36] Priya Singh: No, thanks.
[05:37] Maya Thompson: Thanks everyone.
[05:38] Sarah Patel: Great, meeting adjourned.
